title: investigator-triage-workbench-notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick notes and rough wireframes for a dedicated Investigator / Triage workbench in the Console — focused on helping engineers and support triage timeouts, 5xx, and model runtime errors across routes and deployments. This doc is intentionally informal: sketches, hypotheses, query examples, and a prioritized backlog for grooming.

Problem statement:
- Current error pages are scattershot: per-route tables, raw logs, and occasional replay links. Hard to form hypotheses quickly.
- On-call needs: fast triage, high-confidence mitigations (fallback to smaller model, lower concurrency), and a way to mark incidents as mitigated.
- Product / SRE needs: aggregated error trends across model variants, the ability to reproducibly replay failing requests, and to see unit economics impact of errors (wasted tokens/cost).

Goals (what success looks like):
- <1 min to form a primary hypothesis for any error spike (timeouts / 5xx / model error).
- One-click replay for a representative sample of requests, with sanitized inputs.
- Quick mitigation actions surfaced (route fallback, autoscale boost, degrade quantization) with audited changes.
- Surface root-cause signals: model variant, GPU type, queueing latency, KV cache hit rate, prefix length distribution.

Primary users / personas:
- Platform eng on-call: needs fast actions and audit trail.
- Solutions / support: wants clear repros and customer-friendly summaries.
- ML infra/product: needs data to tune kernels/quantization and to prioritize fixes.

Key flows (happy path):
1) On-call receives alert for increased 5xx on route /payments/resolve.
2) Open Investigator: default view shows aggregated error cards (by error class, model variant, region).
3) Click the 5xx card -> timeline scrubber + waterfall of slow spans + top 5 representative requests.
4) Replay button on representative request opens ephemeral sandbox (sanitized, new model seed) and streams output.
5) If reproducible, select mitigation: route fallback to smaller quantized variant or pin previous stable model. Action is applied and an audit entry is created.

Wireframe (text sketch) — vertical panes, left-to-right:
- Left rail: Context + filters (time window, route, model, region, customer tier, trace id).
- Center: Aggregated Error Cards (grid) — each card = {error class, count, % of total, top contributing model/region, median latency, cost lost estimate}. Click expands.
- Right: Detail panel (timeline scrubber at top, trace waterfall beneath, request list with quick replay & inspect button).
- Bottom collapsible: Mitigation panel (recommended mitigations, safety checks, runbook links, apply button).

Card behavior notes:
- Cards are sorted by priority score = severity_weight * error_rate_change * customer_impact_factor (configurable).
- Hover shows micro-metrics: 95th latency difference, KV cache miss rate delta, queue length.
- Card expansion loads sample traces (up to 20) and shows hash of input (redacted).

Timeline scrubber interaction:
- Default window = last 60 minutes, zoomable to 7d.
- Hover over spike shows breakdown by model variant and queue wait time.
- Select a span to filter request list to requests in that span.

Representative request selection heuristic (for replay):
- Prioritize failed requests with highest tokens consumed and earliest failure stage (generation vs preproc).
- Ensure diversity: include at least one from each region/model variant implicated.
- Redact PII automatically using existing sanitizer rules; allow manual review before replay.

Replay sandbox constraints:
- Replay must run on isolated sandbox model with deterministic seed when possible.
- Limit token budget (configurable) and rate.
- Capture full runtime logs (kernel selection, quantization path, memory pressure events).

Data required from telemetry/logs (minimum fields):
- timestamp, trace_id, route, model_variant, backend_gpu_type, request_tokens, response_tokens, latency_breakdown {queue, decode, kernel}, status_code, error_message, kv_cache_hit, node_id, region, customer_id (hashed).
- Quick query examples to implement:
  - top_error_variants = SELECT model_variant, count(*) FROM requests WHERE status=5xx AND route='/payments/resolve' GROUP BY model_variant ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 5
  - median_queue_delta = SELECT percentile(queue_ms, 50) FROM requests WHERE window AND status!=200 GROUP BY model_variant

Mitigation ideas (to surface as recommended actions):
- Pin stable model_variant for this route for N minutes (requires review)
- Force fallback: route policy -> smaller model for next X minutes
- Autoscale: temporary GPU pool burst (requires quota check)
- Reduce max concurrency for route (fast, low-risk)
- Enable degraded decoding (disable sampling, shorten max tokens)
- Annotate incident and notify customers via templated message (CS flow)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Error cards exist and correctly group by error class and model_variant (QA with synthetic errors).
- Representative replay works end-to-end for a single sanitized request and returns deterministic result when seed fixed.
- One mitigation action (route fallback) can be applied and audited; rollback is possible.
- Timeline scrubber displays correct aggregates and selecting ranges filters requests.

Backlog grooming (prioritized, rough points):
- P0 (8): Aggregated error cards + filters + sorting by priority score.
- P0 (8): Representative request selection and one-click replay sandbox (sanitizer + isolated model runner).
- P1 (5): Mitigation action: route fallback with audit trail and rollback.
- P1 (3): Timeline scrubber UI + zoom + range selection.
- P2 (3): Cost lost estimate on cards (tokens * price).
- P2 (5): Kernel / runtime signal integration (memory pressure, kernel selection).
- P3 (2): Export to postmortem template + auto-populated runbook links.

Open questions / risks:
- Data freshness: telemetry pipeline must provide near-realtime metrics (< 20s). If not, UI value degrades.
- Replay determinism: stochastic sampling + non-deterministic model ops can make replay flaky; need guardrails.
- Security: replay of customer inputs could leak PII; must enforce strict sanitizer and access checks.
- Cost: sandbox replays and autoscale bursts have real spend implications; gating and approvals required.

Notes-to-self / implementation hints:
- Start by building server-side grouping APIs and a lightweight "card" endpoint that returns priority_score + sample_ids.
- Use existing replay infra from solutions-engineering as a backend; add sandbox layer and auto-redaction.
- For the priority score, expose weights in Console settings for SRE to tweak.
- UX: keep actions reversible and surface impacted customers before applying policies.

Next steps:
- Sync Friday with Evan (telemetry) + Jonah (infra) to validate field availability and expected latency.
- Prototype card API and a tiny React shell to iterate wireframes with mock data.
- Groom P0 tickets and assign owners; prepare security review ticket for replay sandbox.

Appendix: quick mockup wireframe (ASCII)
[Filters] | [Error Cards grid]                       | [Detail panel]
--------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------
(route, model, region) | [5xx] [timeout] [model error] [OOM]          | (timeline)
                      | [card: 5xx] count: 120 (+45%) cost: $320  | Trace waterfall
                      | [card: timeout] count: 88 (+120%)          | Requests: [r1] [r2] [r3]
                      | [card: model error] count: 16              | Mitigations: [fallback] [pin model]

--end doc--
